headline: Revenue grows and earnings nearly double on cost cuts
summary_short: ManpowerGroup's Q3 2026 revenue was $4.84B (+4% y/y, +5% constant currency); diluted EPS was $0.71 and $1.01 excluding one-time items.
summary_long: Revenue rose 4% as reported on strength in Manpower, especially the U.S., while gross profit was flat and selling and administrative expenses fell 2.5%, lifting operating profit 24% to $82.3M. Restructuring, transformation costs, a business sale adjustment and Argentina translation losses cut EPS by $0.30. U.S. Experis returned to growth. Fourth-quarter diluted EPS is guided to $1.03-$1.13 with a 44% tax rate. Becky Frankiewicz becomes CEO on January 1, 2027.
confidence_notes: Net earnings growth (+89%) is computed from $34.1M versus $18.0M; EPS delta from $0.71 versus $0.38. Adjusted EPS excludes restructuring, transformation program costs, a business sale adjustment and Argentina currency translation losses as defined by the company.

drivers.explanation: Strength in the Manpower brand, particularly in the United States, with Experis and Talent Solutions improving sequentially.
Lower selling and administrative expenses reflecting continued cost actions, against flat gross profit.
Reported EPS was reduced by $0.30 from restructuring, transformation costs, a business sale adjustment and Argentina translation losses.
CEO called 2026 an inflection point, citing improving demand, execution and transformation progress.
